details: The US Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.50%-3.75% during its recent meeting but signaled that rates could remain high or even rise further in 2026. This hawkish outlook dampened expectations for near-term rate cuts, leading to continued declines in Bitcoin and Ethereum prices. Higher interest rates typically reduce liquidity in financial markets and make non-yielding assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive to investors.
title: Fed's Hawkish Stance Continues to Pressure Bitcoin, Ethereum

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has cautioned that the increasing adoption of US dollar-denominated stablecoins in Nigeria could weaken demand for the local currency (Naira) and reduce the effectiveness of the country's monetary policy. A recent IMF report highlights stablecoins as a significant cross-border payment channel, driven by local inflation and Naira depreciation.
title: IMF Warns Nigeria's Stablecoin Use May Undermine Naira

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is reportedly preparing a new policy that would allow crypto companies to offer tokenized stocks. These blockchain-based instruments, which track traditional equities, could enable 24/7 trading and instant settlement, potentially revolutionizing stock markets and bringing crypto firms into direct competition with traditional brokerages.
title: US SEC Poised to Allow Blockchain-Based Stock Trading

details: Binance's application for a Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) license in Greece is reportedly facing rejection, which could compromise its access to the broader European market. Suspicions of unofficial interference from the European Central Bank (ECB) are fueling the debate, reflecting the ECB's broader concerns over the systemic integration of cryptocurrencies and private stablecoins into EU financial infrastructures.
title: ECB Influence Suspected in Binance MiCA License Issues
